subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should `getAcpSessionManager()` preserve its released manager-instance identity while the manager itself is hardened, or may this security-boundary change intentionally break that Plugin SDK contract now?
rationale: The branch trades a shipped third-party runtime contract for stronger isolation, and repository policy does not authorize that compatibility decision without ACP/plugin-owner intent.

options.title: Harden manager in place
options.body: Keep the released getter identity, move dependencies behind true runtime-private storage, and project private session state from every public manager result.

options.title: Approve immediate facade break
options.body: Accept the plugin compatibility break explicitly, document migration requirements, and provide upgrade proof for existing ACP plugins.

options.title: Pause for versioned removal
options.body: Defer the facade switch until a coordinated deprecation or major-version boundary can remove the class-instance contract.

recommendation.title: Harden manager in place
recommendation.body: Keep the released getter identity, move dependencies behind true runtime-private storage, and project private session state from every public manager result.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily governs the ACP manager's public contract and security boundary.
